title: The Spire of Highmoor Again
premise: Isandro Okafor, a temple scribe bound by debt to the magicless valley of Highmoor, discovers their own name and tonight's date inscribed in a century-old book of prophecies. Hunted by the usurper Veyra's inquisitors, who believe the prophecy's bearer can reforge the shattered covenant between the mortal realm and the fading spirit-realm of the Spire, Isandro flees the only home they've ever known. Along the way they gather reluctant allies—a disgraced knight, a spirit-child, and a traitor archivist—while learning that their invisibility was engineered by the temple to conceal their true nature as the covenant's living keystone. In the climax atop the Spire of Highmoor, Isandro must choose between restoring their stolen identity and power, or sacrificing both to bind the realms together again; they choose sacrifice, reforging the covenant at the cost of being forgotten by everyone they love, though the final chapter hints that memory, like magic, finds its way back.
about_author: Paloma Delacroix is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing medieval covenant charters before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about people trapped by institutions, and live quietly somewhere with too many unread books.

chapters.title: Ink That Remembers
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Copying damaged ledgers in the temple archive, Isandro finds a prophecy book whose final entry names them and tonight's date. Terror and disbelief war with a lifetime of learned invisibility. The chapter ends as temple bells ring an unscheduled alarm—inquisitors have entered the valley where magic cannot follow. Emotional beat: the shattering of a carefully constructed small life.

chapters.title: The Debt of Quiet Years
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Flashbacks interleave with flight: how the temple bought their debt as a child, why the valley forbids magic, and the Abbot's too-knowing warnings. Isandro hides in the tannery district but realizes the inquisitors aren't searching—they're waiting, as if they know Isandro must come to them. Emotional beat: the vertigo of learning your whole life was a cage built by someone else.

chapters.title: What the Knight Buried
chapters.summary: Serah Vance's POV. A disgraced knight turned smuggler is paid to move 'a scribe' through the mountain pass. She recognizes the temple seal on Isandro's travel writ and nearly abandons them, until inquisitors burn the waystation behind them. Forced together, the two trade half-truths by firelight. Emotional beat: wary, transactional loyalty beginning to take root.

chapters.title: The Child of the Threshold
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. In a border ruin between realms, Isandro and Serah find Wren, a spirit-child stranded when the covenant broke a century ago. Touching Wren triggers Isandro's first vision of the Spire—and the realization that they can see and speak to spirits, impossible for valley-born. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into fear as Isandro accepts the prophecy might be true.

chapters.title: The Usurper's Mercy
chapters.summary: Veyra's POV. The usurper-queen reviews her campaign against the free cities and interrogates the captured Abbot, learning the keystone has fled the valley. Her motive is revealed as more than ambition: she believes a broken covenant is the only way to keep spirits from 'meddling' in mortal rule. Emotional beat: chilling sympathy—an antagonist who thinks she is saving the world.

chapters.title: The Traitor's Library
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. In the free city of Corvane, archivist Dell Maro—once Veyra's teacher—decodes the prophecy for Isandro: they are the covenant's keystone, made flesh and hidden in the magicless valley. But the reforging requires a sacrifice the text names only as 'the self, unmade.' Emotional beat: identity as both revelation and sentence.

chapters.title: Siege Bells at Corvane
chapters.summary: Serah's POV. Veyra's armies arrive sooner than any scout predicted—someone sold the city's defenses. During the evacuation, Serah learns Isandro plans to surrender themselves to buy the cities time, and knocks them unconscious rather than allow it. Wren is captured in the chaos. Emotional beat: loyalty and truth collide—love expressed as betrayal.

chapters.title: The Long Ascent
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV, waking in chains Serah forged to keep them from leaving, as the three climb toward the Spire pursued by inquisitors. Isandro confronts Serah's choice and forgives it, understanding at last that loyalty without truth is just ownership. Wren, held by Veyra below, becomes the bargain chip forcing Isandro upward. Emotional beat: reconciliation forged in honesty.

chapters.title: The Unmaking
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Atop the Spire, Veyra offers a poisoned alternative: take the keystone's power fully, become a god, rule both realms. Isandro refuses, choosing instead the prophecy's true cost—unmaking their self, their name, their memory in every mind—to reforge the covenant as Veyra's armies breach the summit. Emotional beat: the climax of self-sacrifice; power declined at the moment it is finally offered.

chapters.title: A Name Like Morning
chapters.summary: Serah's POV, months later. The realms are knitted together; spirits walk openly, Veyra's army has dissolved, and the free cities honor a nameless savior no one can quite remember. Serah keeps a scribe's worn ink-stained journal she cannot explain owning. In the last scene, Wren speaks a word that isn't a word, and somewhere a stranger looks up as if hearing their own name for the first time. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into hope—identity, like the covenant, reforged.
